articles.title: Author Chloe Gong on ‘Eyes of Kings’ ending, ‘Deadlock’ debut and how she wants ‘These Violent Delights’ adapted for TV or film
articles.summary: Chloe Gong has had a busy 2026. The author best known for her hit 2020 “Romeo & Juliet” retelling “These Violent Delights,” which is set in 1920s Shanghai, released the conclusion of one trilogy series last month and is preparing for the launch of her second book in another series in November, all…
body: “It’s secret because it’s brand new for me. It’s my first venture into something contemporary,” Gong says, “I have been kind of teasing it as, imagine an Emily Henry love story meets the zombie apocalypse. I’m super excited to talk about it more, and I think at this point, I’ve done that teaser enough times that I’m like, it’s OK, my publisher’s not gonna sack me for that.”

Amid her packed writing schedule, Gong has taken some time to view readers’ reactions to the end of “Eyes of Kings” — the final installment in her trilogy inspired by Shakespeare’s “Antony and Cleopatra” — but she says she’s not actively seeking out fans’ hot takes.

While Gong’s projects have yet to be adapted for the big screen, a project based on “These Violent Delights” has been rumored for some time and Gong says there’s still potential for it to move forward.

articles.summary: There has not been a single major industry event in the last three months where major producers and execs have not brought up the phenomenon of Kane Parsons’ “Backrooms” and Curry Barker’s “Obsession.” The two films, directed by 20-something-year-olds who came from YouTube, exploded all box-office…
body: “I’m gonna try to stay as oblivious to those labels as possible,” he added. “I think I have more creative control now with future projects. So those sort of structures will probably be a little less forceful, I think, in the future.”

Speaking of sequels, fellow Zurich Summit panellist Robbie Brenner, president and chief content officer at Mattel Studios, was asked about a possible sequel to Greta Gerwig’s smash hit “Barbie.” Her answer was brief but positive: “Look, we all wanna have a ‘Barbie’ sequel. I mean, who doesn’t wanna see the sequel to ‘Barbie’? And I’m sure at some point in time there will be one. We all want it to happen. We’ll see.”

Young maverick Parsons stood as the spokesperson for his generation in a panel next to industry titans: Brenner as well as Michael Barker, co-president of Sony Pictures Classics, and Bill Kramer, CEO of the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences. Parsons said he did not want to make it “too much of an age thing” but that there is a clear “appetite” for the theatrical experience at the moment.

articles.title: ‘Ghost Song’ Review: Fatih Akin Doesn’t Find Top Form in This Supernatural Romance, but at Least It Has Beautiful Ghosts
articles.summary: Since hitting an artistic peak with the back-to-back festival triumphs “Head-On” and “Edge of Heaven” in the mid-2000s, German-Turkish auteur Fatih Akin has darted all over the map in genre, style and form — occasionally striking commercially, as with the Diane Kruger thriller “In the Fade” and the…
body: Separated by tragedy on the night they meet, two young graduates continue their relationship anyway in this thin but radiantly shot 'Wings of Desire' riff.

Farasha (luminous first-timer Mariam Dawoud) is a Syrian refugee who has settled and assimilated in Hamburg with her family, following an interstitial stint in Turkey. Though she chooses to wear a traditional headscarf, in other respects she lives as a modern, independent-minded woman, following in the footsteps of her late father by studying physics at university, while keeping at least one haram secret that would scandalize her mother: a butterfly tattoo on her stomach.

At a graduation party in Hamburg’s imposing Telemichel tower, she meets and immediately sparks with fellow grad Faris (Eren M. Guvercin), a tousle-haired, German-born Muslim of Turkish descent. With her very tipsy bestie Una (Carlotta von Falkenhayn), they decide to continue the party elsewhere and pile into his car; in circumstances deliberately (and somewhat luridly) parceled out over the course of the film, an accident sees the vehicle plunge into the Elbe river.

articles.title: Jonathan Lipnicki on His Bold Role Opposite Robert Pattinson in ‘Primetime’ and Why He Left L.A.
articles.summary: The former child star — famous for telling Tom Cruise "a human head weighs eight pounds" in 'Jerry Maguire' — opens up about baring all in the Lance Oppenheim-directed film, being brave and staying stubborn for what he loves most: "I don't quit."
body: A little more than a year ago, Jonathan Lipnicki started praying nightly for clarity in his career.

It worked. Not long after, Lipnicki arrived at a new gig, and while it didn’t deliver the most amount of screen time in his lengthy IMDb credits, it delivered the boldest turn of the 35-year-old’s career. Lipnicki — a beloved child star who, at age 6, hit the jackpot by making his debut opposite Tom Cruise and Renée Zellweger in Cameron Crowe’s Jerry Maguire before moving on to other hits like Stuart Little — snagged a part in Lance Oppenheim ‘s Primetime for A24.

That applies to Lipnicki, who shed more than that — specifically, his pants — for a full frontal scene complete with a can of whipped cream. “As actors, we pray for dark material and for things we can really sink our teeth into. At the end of the day, you have to ask yourself, ‘Am I as courageous an artist as I say I am?’ I had to answer that question, and I was courageous enough to take the plunge,” Lipnicki told The Hollywood Reporter over Zoom in September. “I’ve tried to live by the idea that, when it comes to art, if something scares you, most likely you should do it.”

articles.title: Kane Parsons Recalls ‘Backrooms’ Trailer “Activated a Desire to See: How Did Hollywood Mess This Up?”
articles.summary: Luckily, the young filmmaker told the Zurich Summit that he likes to think he did the core idea of his iconic YouTube series justice — and touched on the possibility of a sequel.
body: Twenty-one-year-old Kane Parsons is reflecting on a whirlwind summer in which the box office was undoubtedly bolstered by the release of his feature debut, Backrooms.

Speaking with some of the industry’s top executives at the Zurich Film Festival Summit on Saturday afternoon, the young director spoke about the health of the 2026 box office, which has catapulted YouTube natives Parsons and Obsession ‘s Curry Barker to the top of Hollywood.

Parsons actually confessed he doesn’t think of A24’s Backrooms, starring Renate Reinsve and Chiwetel Ejiofor, as a traditional horror film. “I didn’t direct it like a horror film. I don’t view it as a horror project. I think that’s just naturally the path of least resistance from a marketing perspective, and it’s what seems comfortable to people as a framing device,” he said. “But I’m going to try to stay as oblivious to those labels as possible, and just focus on [what] think I have greater control now with future projects, so those sort of structures [should] probably be a little less forceful, I think.”

articles.title: Star Trek: Strange New Worlds' Controversial Season 4 Is A Celebration Of TV Long Gone
articles.summary: Star Trek: Strange New Worlds Season 4 earned its fair share of controversy, but its ambitious storytelling approach felt like a throwback to an earlier TV era.
body: "Star Trek: Strange New Worlds" is a delightful show that captures the heart of "The Original Series" while updating its visuals and humor for modern audiences. If you've never watched a "Star Trek" show, this is the perfect entry point to the franchise. It has the right balance of serialization and episodic storytelling, with each episode serving as its own unique and self-contained adventure while still pushing a larger narrative.

Season 4 was no different — it's a grab bag of sci-fi delights where every episode hits a different tone and adopts an entirely different genre style. One week you'd see the crew of the Enterprise being hunted by dinosaurs, and the next might just be a haunted house horror episode. As great as this season was, however, it wasn't without some controversy. Specifically, some fans complained about the number of gimmick episodes (via Reddit ), claiming that the show spends too much time exploring new genres rather than establishing its own.
points: Star Trek: Strange New Worlds Season 4 earned its fair share of controversy, but its ambitious storytelling approach felt like a throwback to an earlier TV era.

articles.title: Academy CEO Bill Kramer Doubles Down on YouTube Move: “You’ll See a Very Different-Looking Oscars”
articles.summary: Kramer said at the Zurich Film Festival Summit on Saturday afternoon that bringing Hollywood's biggest night to YouTube "gives the Academy more control in engaging with film lovers."
body: Does AMPAS CEO Bill Kramer feel as though they’re taking a risk by moving the awards ceremony to YouTube in 2029?
“It almost feels risky not to do it,” said Kramer at the Zurich Film Festival Summit event on Saturday afternoon.

Following Kramer’s keynote speech at the Swiss summit, he doubled down on taking the Oscars — which has aired on ABC in the U.S. since 1976 — to YouTube, in a deal that will bring the film industry’s biggest night to millions more people, translated into 30 different languages, for free.

He told the room: “As we become more global as an organization, the best way for us to reach a global audience of film lovers, film fans, [and] young artists is YouTube. I think the timing this year — Obsession, Backrooms, you and Curry [Barker],” he said, talking to Parsons. “[It’s] moving in the other direction from YouTube to theatrical for us; we’re an organization that celebrates theatrical filmmaking, but at the same time, the Oscars is a television show, and we want to reach a large audience.”

articles.title: Werwulf Trailer: Robert Eggers' New Horror Movie Looks Like The Perfect Nosferatu Companion
articles.summary: Get ready to bark at the moon with Aaron Taylor-Johnson in the latest spooky trailer for Robert Eggers' Werwulf, due out this Christmas.
body: Robert Eggers is the Wes Anderson of horror. Like Anderson, he has a distinct style he has no interest in shying away from, a stable of actors he wants to keep working with (bonus: both of those stables include Willem Dafoe), and, at this point, you either love him or hate him. I'm in the former camp: I've been all-in on old Bobby Eggs since "The Witch" arrived and introduced the world to Black Phillip. Since then, I've been on board with all of Eggers' movies (although I'll confess I was a tad mixed on "The Northman").

Back around Christmas 2024, Eggers scored a big hit — his highest grossing film to date — with the genuinely scary fever dream "Nosferatu." Now, he's back to give us another holiday horror release with "Werwulf." The film's latest trailer is here, and, yep, it sure looks like a Robert Eggers movie. (I mean that as a compliment, but your mileage may vary.) Set in the 13th century, "Werwulf" stars Aaron Taylor-Johnson as a farmer who turns into a beast, unleashing all sorts of horrors upon those around him. Check out the movie's new trailer above.

articles.title: 10 Best Returning TV Shows Of 2026 (So Far)
articles.summary: Plenty of new shows debuted in 2026, but these are the best shows that returned with a new season, some of which are wrapping things up.
body: In a particularly tumultuous year for the entertainment industry, 2026 has already seen its fair share of television cancellations. Sometimes it feels like a rare privilege when a show gets to run for multiple seasons, particularly in this mercurial streaming era. It's even rarer when a show returns and is roughly just as good as it was when audiences last saw it. With that in mind, we're highlighting our favorite established shows that returned with new episodes throughout 2026.

From episodes launching a new season after a lengthy hiatus to shows maintaining a regular production schedule, these are ones that proved to be worth the wait. Whether it's a hit animated series with a fresh batch of episodes or gripping streaming dramas, we had a lot to thankfully choose from this year. There's always something special in seeing fan-favorite characters light up the screen again, something we've grown to appreciate more with how unpredictable the industry is these days.
Here are the 10 best returning TV shows of 2026 so far, each retaining the quality that made audiences fall in love with them in the first place.
